question: The Santhal Revolt of 1855-56 was against which groups along with the British officials?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zamindars and moneylenders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Santhal Revolt was a tribal uprising that took place between **1855-56** in present-day Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• The rebellion was primarily directed against the **exploitative practices of zamindars and moneylenders**, who oppressed the Santhal community through exorbitant taxes and loans.
 
• The **British colonial officials supported the zamindars**, further exacerbating the exploitation of the tribal population.
 
• Leaders of the revolt, **Sido and Kanhu Murmu**, mobilized thousands of Santhals to fight against the injustices.
 
• The revolt was eventually suppressed by the British forces, but it remains a significant event in Indian history as one of the earliest organized rebellions against colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santhals:**

 
 
• The Santhals are one of the largest tribal communities in India, predominantly residing in Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• They have a rich cultural heritage with distinct traditions, language (Santhali), and lifestyle.
 
 
 
• **Causes of the Revolt:**
 
 
• The primary reason for the revolt was the exploitation of the Santhal community by zamindars and moneylenders through unfair taxation and loans.
 
• British policies, such as the Permanent Settlement, worsened the plight of the tribal population.
 
 
 
• **Sido and Kanhu Murmu:**
 
 
• These were the key leaders of the Santhal Revolt, who emerged as symbols of resistance against colonial oppression.
 
• They organized the tribal population and initiated the uprising in June 1855.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the Revolt:**
 
 
• The Santhal Revolt highlighted the plight of tribal communities under British rule and their resistance against exploitation.
 
• It laid the foundation for subsequent tribal and peasant movements in India.
